# Brevi

> Brevi is experimental and archived: of the ten most-downloaded Python MCP servers on PyPI, built unchanged on 19 Nov 2026 with Brevi 0.28.3, none built natively (report: https://github.com/ets-public/brevi/blob/main/bench/showcase/REAL_SERVERS.md). It is no longer developed and is not recommended for new projects. What follows describes what it does on the programs it does build. Brevi turns a small Python MCP server or CLI script into one native binary that needs no Python on the machine that runs it, and starts fast. Build with `brevi build server.py --release -o my-server`, then register it with `claude mcp add my-server -- ./my-server`; for a CLI, `brevi build tool.py --release -o tool`. Brevi is a compiler, written in Rust, that compiles Python through Rust; a program it builds itself links no libpython. Measured on Brevi 0.26.0 (commit 69caf93, 10 Nov 2026), Linux x86-64, Intel Xeon 2.10 GHz, 4 cores, median of 10 runs, CPython 3.13, same output byte for byte: the official mcp-server-time 2026.11.4, unchanged, answers its first tool call in 35 ms against 730 ms on CPython (19.2 MB binary); an SQLite MCP server on the official mcp SDK takes 27 ms against 718 ms (18.0 MB); a one-file tiktoken token counter takes 33 ms against 375 ms (11.5 MB). The win is start-up and import time, not throughput: the same counter over a whole source tree is 2.2x faster, and the dynamic build most programs take runs at about CPython's speed (median 0.85x). Limits: an import Brevi does not build itself (pandas, yaml) runs in CPython through a bridge, so that binary needs Python 3.13 and the packages it was built against on the run machine, or `--standalone` (Linux and Windows; it misses lazily imported packages), and loses the fast start. Most real MCP servers take this path today: of the ten most-downloaded Python MCP servers on PyPI, built unchanged on 19 Nov 2026 with Brevi 0.28.3, none built natively, all ten started at 1.00x to 1.16x CPython's time, and `--standalone` broke 4 of them (https://github.com/ets-public/brevi/blob/main/bench/showcase/REAL_SERVERS.md); mcp-server-time 2026.11.18 also no longer builds natively; Linux binaries link the system glibc dynamically, so build on the oldest Linux you target; macOS programs are not tested by CI and Windows is beta; some memory is not freed yet, so watch a server that runs for days. Brevi is a preview: not every server builds, and when one does not, the build says why in one JSON line. Binary sizes are not tuned yet. Secondary features: `brevi run --verify main.py` checks a run against CPython, `brevi check` reports sure mistakes as one short JSON line with a suggested fix, and `brevi mcp` serves these to coding agents.

Security: no external security audit yet. The sandbox (`--sandbox`, on by default in the MCP tools and the SDKs) is a policy layer, not an isolation boundary. Run untrusted code in a container or VM. `--allow-py` and `--allow native` are full trust.

## Docs

- [Ship an MCP server or CLI as one binary](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/bundle-mcp.md): the full guide: build, register with Claude Code, size, start time and limits.
- [Quickstart](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/quickstart.md): install, build an MCP server and a CLI as binaries, then the short loop for coding agents.
- [FAQ](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/faq.md): does the run machine need Python, binary size, start time, which servers build, and how it differs from PyInstaller, Nuitka and zipapp.
- [Showcases](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/showcases.md): real MCP servers and CLIs built unchanged, timed against CPython, with size and whether they need Python.
- [Install](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/install.md): uvx, uv tool, the install script, pip, npm, Docker and building from source.
- [Using Brevi](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/usage.md): commands, flags, error formats, which path ran (typed, dynamic, pybridge or CPython) and why, the CPython fallback, sandbox and GUI test mode.
- [What builds, and limits](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/compatibility.md): what runs native, what needs CPython, what is refused, and the conformance numbers.
- [For AI agents](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/agents.md): the MCP server's tools, the skill and plugin, and prompting advice.
- [Agent skill](https://brevi-lang.org/skill.md): setup and the write, run, fix loop for coding agents.
- [Architecture](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/architecture.md): how a source file becomes a native program.
- [Language guide](https://brevi-lang.org/guide.md): Brevi's own syntax, for .bv files only. Not needed to build Python.
- [Reference](https://brevi-lang.org/reference.md): details for string braces and format specs, list methods and Python spellings. Look up one name with `brevi guide WORD` instead of reading it all.
- [Libraries](https://brevi-lang.org/libraries.md): using other .bv files, Rust crates (`use sha2 "0.10"` plus `rust fn`) and Python (`py fn`) from Brevi.
- [Changelog](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/changelog.md): what changed in each release, and what is on main for the next.
- [Benchmarks](https://brevi-lang.org/bench.md): speed against CPython and cost per finished task, with method and raw logs.

## Tools

- [Compiler source](https://github.com/ets-public/brevi): Apache-2.0, written in Rust.
- [Agent platform templates](https://github.com/ets-public/brevi/tree/main/templates): run an agent's Python under Brevi's sandbox and limits on E2B, Daytona, Modal, Cloudflare Sandbox or Docker.
- Contact: support@brevi-lang.org (questions, licensing; bugs go to GitHub issues).

- [Full text](https://brevi-lang.org/llms-full.txt): the guide, reference, libraries and skill in one file.
